title: Cults of blood
summary: Mortal followings gathered by Cainites around 1215.

claims.text: Cainites gather mortal cults for nourishment, knowledge, obedience, indulgence or temporal power, and some elders run cults that worship them outright.
Recruits are cut off from outside contact and then shaped, given small secret tasks with reward for success and punishment for failure.
Dominate forces obedience without winning loyalty and can leave followers frightened, resentful or without will of their own; Presence keeps free will but needs a light touch.
The blood oath is held up as the surest way to bind a cult’s inner circle.

title: The Cult Background
summary: Rating a cult with cult points.

claims.text: Each dot of the Cult Background gives one cult point, five at most, to build a cult with Storyteller approval.
A cult is described by six Traits: Size, Influence, Loyalty, Resources, Secrecy and Arcana; some carry negative values that free points for others.
Size runs from 0 points for about ten members up to 6 for a thousand, with larger cults rare and usually off limits to players.
Influence runs from none, through a town or monastery, a city, a barony and a county or diocese, to a whole nation or all of the Church.
Loyalty must be kept up through rites, contact with followers and Disciplines, and ranges from Divided at -2 through Opportunistic and Fairly Loyal upward.

title: The Cult of Mithras
summary: A warrior cult led by the Ventrue Methuselah Mithras.

claims.text: The cult claims to continue an ancient pagan faith from before Christ and draws soldiers and generals; its god walks among them as the Ventrue Methuselah Mithras.
Mithras woke from torpor near the Scottish border after the Norman invasion of 1066.
A temple raised to Mithras in London was burned by the local clergy with Ventrue backing, killing those inside, though Mithras and some followers escaped.
Based in England, the cult reaches into Wales, Scotland and Aquitaine.

title: The Masons of Marseilles
summary: A secretive builders’ guild used by Cainites.

claims.text: Guilds of the masons who build castles and cathedrals guard their trade secrets, and that secrecy suits Cainites with secrets of their own.
In Marseilles, a port where many crusaders took ship, returning men brought back lore of the holy sites of Jerusalem to the guild.
The Marseilles guild has reach among other Masonic guilds in France and Italy.

title: The Followers of Lazarus
summary: A scattered cult honouring the Cappadocian Lazarus.

claims.text: Lazarites hold the Cappadocian Lazarus to be wise and divine and study life and death to imitate and serve that elder.
Constancia, high priestess at Erciyes, calls them heretics because Lazarus defied Cappadocius and because they believe in resurrection.
Some say Lazarus is the man of the Gospel, Embraced before being raised by Christ, a blessing said to grant a new state and deep insight into death.
Lazarus later studied death in Egypt, including the funeral rites of the Egyptians, and visited the Great Library of Alexandria.

title: House Goratrix
summary: A faction within Clan Tremere around the exiled Goratrix.

claims.text: Not long after House Tremere became a clan of vampires, blood rites, demonic pacts and charges of treachery began to spread within it.
Goratrix, sent to Paris on the excuse of watching occult matters, nurses anger at the exile and plots a coup.
Goratrix works to turn Thaumaturgy toward a black art, and the faction has members at Ceoris, in Transylvania and across Europe and the Levant.

title: Calomena’s Forsaken
summary: A vampiric cult in the Balkans.

claims.text: Before the sack of Constantinople in the Fourth Crusade, the city was plagued by a vampiric cult called the Chosen of Calomena.
Its remnant, Calomena’s Forsaken, now moves through the Balkans.

title: The Church on the blood cults
summary: How a Church investigator describes Cainite cults.

claims.text: An inquisitor’s report describes cults that venerate and drink blood, shun meat and are said to have power over beasts, loyalties and lightning.
The report notes that sunlight burns these beings and fire drives them to terror, and that they name themselves Vampyr and claim descent from Cain.
It describes them as one quarrelsome cult with ranks, the most corpselike sitting highest, and some new ones still able to walk by day.
